item.title: Who are all you people
item.content:encoded:
I only just remembered this scp existed, nine years after i wrote it. It's surreal to see my mediocre writing be one of the top rated SCP pages and have four pages of discussion and there literally being fan art of the locket itself.

I'm tempted to stay silent since it's nice for a work to just exist, but i also wanted to clear some stuff up.

-those lines being from system shock 2; i was very surprised to hear that since i have only played about an hour of system shock 2 (i know, i'll get to it one day) and just thought up some generic creepy lines for the flesh beast to say as it ascended beyond human thought boundaries.
-the safe/keter distinction was made based on the very early ways in which things were classified which i guess has matured a lot over time, and i remember a few other SCPs at the time making the classification split so i followed along with that. Also because the flesh beasts are terribly aggressive, very lethal, and extremely durable
-the term lovecraftian is used just because of the creature's similarities to shoggoths

Man, i kind of want to go back and clean it up, and write a new class D interview which doesn't sound as generic but there's something to be said about leaving well enough alone

item.content:encoded:
I don't see how they pose a threat to life as we know it.

Although the Object Classes page does state something to that effect, generally people apply the "locked box test": if you put it in a box and

1. it won't do anything, it's Safe.
2. you're not that sure it won't escape and hurt someone, it's Euclid.
3. it will actively try to escape the box and maybe eat your face when it sees you, it's Keter.

The second-to-last paragraph of this article is a pretty clear indication why the flesh beasts are Keter.
